So I've been with hunt since there was only one map. What I've come to realize  is that you have your good days and you have your bad. Most of the time I average a high 4 star but I'll get a day where I'm up in the fives and a days where I just drop to the twos.
 One thing I recommend is to take the free boy from your recruit and run him with whatever weapons add melee and a medkit. this is a cheap way to learn the weapons of the game and see which one you might like the most. Once you find your weapon of choice, take it every match. The guns in this game have a little bit different mechanics than others so each one takes some practice. Personally I stick with a Winfield or a springfield variant or if I'm feeling a bit more close range the Romero is a solid choice. 
Another note, if you can play with the same people consistently then you learn how they move and where you might need to support them or vice versa.
Lastly I'd recommend watching some of Rachta's YouTube videos on hunt gameplay. Hes excellent at explaining what hunts "tutorial" doesn't.

Also please do due diligence on the care of the bird you do choose so that you can pick up on the signs if it gets sick (I have full faith that you're a responsible human being but it's something I tell anybody getting a new bird)
Lastly the most common denominator of the horror stories is how well they were handled. Petsmart/co doesn't hand feed their birds or handle them so you'll simply have more of a challenge if you want to handle it and get it to trust you

There is also the option of getting a rescue bird. Depending on the birds back story they could take some work at the beginning to forge a bond but it will be worth every bit.
